# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: DECFRA Pch through GL/GR and the designated sets; DECCRA overlap and self copy
# Run by tests/rect_fixes.rs (`decfra_charset_spec_rows`) through tests/spec/mod.rs, whole and byte by byte  (task 24.14, refs #489 #461)
#
# Same layout as charset_spec.txt (### ID / size / step / cite / note / screen / cursor / pending_wrap / requests /
# scrollback), parseable by tests/spec/mod.rs once pointed at this file. Extra keys the shared parser ignores:
#   flags: decision | xterm-quirk | control | invisible    (decision = a lead ruling, 2026-11-17; Tessera's behaviour is in `screen`)
#   xterm_screen: what xterm shows when it differs from `screen` (documentation only)
#   cells: code points of the filled cells for rows whose glyph is invisible (NBSP, soft hyphen)
# Cursor is 0-based (row,col); render_screen puts `|` AFTER the cursor's cell. Non-ASCII payload is written \u{..};
# expected screens are literal characters. Every row fills columns 1-3 of row 1 with `CSI Pch;1;1;1;3 $ x` unless noted.
# Tessera is always UTF-8; the terminal starts at level 4 (Terminal::new, VT400-class; tests/rect_fixes.rs also checks level 5), DECNRCM off unless a row says so.
#
# SOURCES (all fetched this run)
#   [CTL]    xterm ctlseqs  https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html
#            "CSI Pc;Pt;Pl;Pb;Pr $ x  Fill Rectangular Area (DECFRA), VT420 and up. Pc is the character to use."  (no range, no GL/GR text)
#            "CSI Pt;Pl;Pb;Pr;Pp;Pt;Pl;Pp $ v  Copy Rectangular Area (DECCRA)"  (nothing on overlap)
#   [XT-cp]  xterm charproc.c (ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots master) CASE_DECFRA (~line 5666) and current_charset() (~1785):
#              value = use_default_value(0, ' ');            /* Pch <= 0 or absent -> space */
#              /* DEC 070, page 5-170 says the fill-character is either ASCII or Latin1; xterm allows printable Unicode values. */
#              if (nparam > 0 && ((value >= 256 && CharWidth(screen, value) > 0) || IsLatin1(screen, value)))
#                  ScrnFillRectangle(xw, &rect, value, current_charset(screen, value), xw->flags, True);
#              current_charset(): result = nrc_ASCII; if IsLatin1(value): curss != 0 ? gsets[curss]
#                                 : value >= 0x80 ? gsets[curgr] : gsets[curgl]
#              IsLatin1(n) = (32 <= n <= 126) || (160 <= n <= 255)   [Upper8Bits = 160 unless allowC1Printable, then 128]  (xterm.h)
#              CSI state does SetParam(nparam++, DEFAULT), so nparam >= 1 even for a bare `CSI $ x`.
#   [XT-scr] xterm screen.c ScrnFillRectangle(): `if (charset != nrc_ASCII) { write_text = &actual; if (xtermCharSetOut(xw,1,charset)==0) actual = ' '; }`
#            then writes `actual` to every cell of the rectangle (translation happens BEFORE any width test; there is no width test).
#            screen.c ScrnCopyRectangle(): "make a local copy of the source rectangle first, then apply the target from that"
#            (newCellData(size) of the whole source rectangle); target = parsed Ptd;Pld, sized like the source, clipped by the
#            `col <= getMaxCol` / `row <= getMaxRow` guards in the write loop; pages ignored.
#   [XT-cs]  xterm charsets.c xtermCharSetOut(): cs = (eight >= 128) ? gsets[curgr] : leftset (the set passed in, = current_charset);
#            seven = eight & 0x7f; skipped for code points > 0xFF in UTF-8; DEC Special Graphic: seven 0x60..0x7E -> dec2ucs, `chr == 0x5f` (the
#            UNMASKED code) -> 0, else chr = seven; DEC Supplemental/Technical via map_DEC_Supp_Graphic / map_DEC_Technical (UNI entries active:
#            begin_CODEPAGE bumps utf8_nrc_mode unless DECNRCM is on); DEL (chr == 0x7f) in a seven-bit set is REMOVED and `count` drops to 0 -
#            which makes ScrnFillRectangle fill a SPACE; afterwards `if (eight >= 128 && chr < 128 && chr > 32) chr |= 128`.
#   [XT-tbl] xterm charsets.h: UNDEF = 0x2426; map_DEC_Supp_Graphic 0x24/0x26/0x2C-0x2F/0x34/0x38/0x3E/0x50/0x5E/0x70/0x7E -> U+2426,
#            0x28 -> U+00A4, 0x57 -> U+0152, 0x5D -> U+0178, 0x77 -> U+0153, 0x7D -> U+00FF; map_DEC_Technical 0x2D -> U+23AB.
#   [VT510]  https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECFRA.html : "Pch can be any value from 32 to 126 or from 160 to 255. If Pch is not in this
#            range, then the terminal ignores the DECFRA command. The decimal value refers to the character in the current GL or GR in-use
#            table." / "The fill character assumes the visual character attributes set by the last SGR" / "DECFRA does not change the
#            current line attributes" / "does not change the active cursor position" / out-of-page values are clamped / VT level 4 only.
#            https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECCRA.html : "retains its character values and attributes"; "If the destination area is
#            partially off the page, then DECCRA clips the off-page data"; page 4 DOES NOT SAY how overlap is handled; the text's
#            "If Pbs is greater than Pts" is a typo for Pts > Pbs; DECOM affects coordinates; margins do not.
#   [DEC070] DEC STD 070 (the video systems reference) p. 5-170 as quoted by the xterm comment above: fill character is ASCII or Latin-1.
#            Not fetched directly (not online); only the quote in [XT-cp] is relied on.
#   [TESS]   crates/tessera-term/src/rect.rs fill_char() (HEAD a4c1408), tests/rect_fixes.rs, tests/rect.rs Q4, docs/adr/0046 amendment
#            "DECFRA mapping order and the exact self copy (#269)", crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/charset_spec.txt (rows GR*, SG*, SU*, SS*).
#   kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, iTerm2: not cited. Alacritty and kitty do not implement DECFRA at all (from memory, not verified here);
#   iTerm2 implements DECFRA/DECCRA/DECERA (from memory, not verified here). xterm and the DEC manuals are the oracle.
#
# STATE OF THE BRIEF vs main (read this first)
#   The DECFRA "translate, then check" defect, the exact DECCRA self copy and the app-core damage test ALL ALREADY LIVE on main:
#   rect.rs fill_char() maps through the sets and then calls fillable(); tests/rect_fixes.rs has the exhaustive 191x24x2x2 table;
#   tests/rect_alloc.rs checks the self copy; crates/tessera-app-core/tests/rect_damage.rs EXISTS (not new). ADR 0046 has the
#   amendment. What is left of "DECFRA" is: the decisions D-SS, D-DROP, D-SHY, D-WIDE below (Tessera vs xterm), the differential
#   volume bar (rect_fixes.rs compares 36,672 cases; the brief wants >= 10M random), and a mutation check.
#
# DECISIONS (the lead's rulings of 2026-11-17: D-GR through GR, D-SS follows xterm, D-DROP / D-SHY / D-WIDE keep Tessera; ADR 0046)
#   D-GR     Do Pch 160-255 map through GR or are they Latin-1? -> THROUGH GR. [VT510] "refers to the character in the current GL or GR
#            in-use table"; [XT-cp] current_charset() uses gsets[curgr]. With the default GR (ASCII in UTF-8) the mapping is the identity, so
#            "Latin-1" is the special case, not an alternative. Tessera already does this (rows C01-C12).
#   D-SS     A pending single shift (SS2/SS3) when DECFRA arrives: xterm uses the shifted set for Pch 32-126 (current_charset: curss != 0 ->
#            gsets[curss]) and leaves it pending (CASE_DECFRA never clears curss). Tessera uses GL and also leaves it pending (rect.rs
#            `Charsets::from(saved())`, tests/rect.rs q4). Recommend xterm: it is what "fills with the character printing the same byte would
#            write" means, and what the brief's differential should then include. Costs one `single_shift` copy in fill_char(). Row D01.
#   D-DROP   A Pch that printing DROPS (255 under a seven-bit GR set, i.e. DEL after mapping): xterm fills a SPACE (count 0 -> ' '); Tessera
#            ignores the sequence. Recommend KEEP Tessera (nothing), which is what the brief's "writes nothing where print writes nothing" and
#            security.md's "never writes a C0, C1 or DEL cell" say; document the xterm deviation in ADR 0046. Row C04.
#   D-SHY    Pch 173 with ASCII (or any set that leaves it U+00AD): xterm fills U+00AD (CharWidth(173) is 1 for any Latin-1 value); Tessera
#            ignores it (U+00AD is zero width, so printing it writes no cell). Recommend KEEP Tessera: a zero-width fill cell breaks the
#            one-column cell model; same class as D-WIDE. Row A09.
#   D-WIDE   Pch >= 256 that is a wide character: xterm fills it into every cell (CharWidth > 0 accepts width 2, no HIDDEN_CHAR pairing,
#            so the screen holds overlapping double-width glyphs); Tessera requires width 1. Recommend KEEP Tessera. Row A13.
#   D-NOPARAM `CSI $ x` with no Pch at all: xterm fills the whole screen with spaces (nparam >= 1); Tessera does the same. Same result, no
#            decision needed (row A15); listed because the brief's "Pch absent is a space" is right.
#
# THINGS THE BRIEF / ISSUE TEXT GETS WRONG
#   - "DECFRA (20.1 adversarial M1, real defect): fill_char tests fillable(U+00AD) before translating": already fixed on main (see above).
#   - "crates/tessera-app-core/tests/rect_damage.rs (new)": the file exists (2 tests: damage like EL, selection cleared like after EL).
#   - "20.1 adv M2: DECCRA self-copy cost already fixed": true; the doc says so in rect.rs, grid rect.rs, ADR 0046 and security.md.
#   - "20.1 n2 take() moves the entry Vec out": rect.rs L55-57, grid rect.rs L28 and security.md already say it.
#   - The 34.7M-case differential is not in the repo; rect_fixes.rs does 36,672 cases (24 sets x GL/GR x DECNRCM x 191 Pch). The sets with
#     NRCS finals K Y E 6 Z 7 H = 9 ` %6 are in; only ISO Latin-2/5/Greek/Hebrew/Cyrillic and JIS are not implemented at all, so a
#     bigger run can only add the G0-G3 x GL/GR x single-shift x DECNRCM x level state space (G1 alone is covered today), not more sets.
#   - Whether xterm "treats Pch 160-255 as Latin-1": it does for acceptance (IsLatin1), and maps through GR for the glyph.
#
# =============================================================================
